function: p. 1-2: Learned compression and reconstruction of the CSI matrix for feedback in near-field XL-MIMO, with an encoder at the user and a decoder at the base station (ExtendNLNet).
system: p. 4: Near-field XL-MIMO downlink, base station with N1 = 1024 antennas, user with N2 = 1 antenna, no RIS, free-space spherical-wave channel; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 2-3: ExtendNLNet, a convolutional encoder-decoder with Non-Local and Refine-net blocks, trained end to end with supervised MSE loss at compression ratios 16, 32 and 64.
data_channel: p. 2, 4: Own simulated near-field free-space channel H(r, theta, phi), Eq. 6; 25,000 training, 5,000 test and 5,000 validation samples; no standard model or measurement.
test_conditions: p. 4: Training, validation and test sets come from the same simulated channel; one network per compression ratio (Table I); 100 epochs, batch 250, learning rate 0.001.
baselines: p. 4: Learned only: CsiNet and Attention-CsiNet; no non-learned method such as codebook or compressive sensing is compared.
metrics: p. 4: NMSE (dB) and cosine similarity rho versus compression ratio (Table II), and NMSE or rho training curves versus epoch (Figs. 4-7).
complexity: p. 4: Number of parameters (Table I): ExtendNLNet 543,456, 281,248 and 150,144 at CR 16, 32 and 64; CsiNet 530,656, 268,448 and 137,344.
openness: p. 1-5: none; no link to code or data is given.
q1_support: p. 2: "under the assumption of geometric free-space propagation [18]"; the channel of Eq. 2-6 is the paper's own analytical near-field model, and no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 4: "The number of samples in the training set, test set, and validation set are 25,000, 5,000, and 5,000, respectively"; the test set is a held-out part of the same data, and no new scenario or configuration is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "we have compared the performance of CsiNet, Attention-CsiNet, and ExtendNLNet"; both baselines are learned, and no non-learned method is compared although p. 1 mentions codebook and compressive-sensing methods.
q4_support: p. 4: "we use the number of parameters to express the complexity of the networks" (Table I gives the counts).
q5_support: p. 2: "under the assumption of geometric free-space propagation [18]"; the data are self-generated, and no page gives a code or data link or a public dataset.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv preprint 2405.09053v2 (23 May 2024); it prints no DOI, so the match with the DOI rests on the title and the letter format. The paper states no carrier frequency and no distribution of user distance or angles for the samples. Pages 3-4 were also checked as images for Tables I-II and the figures.
